entries.name: Easter
entries.capsule: The Christian feast of the Resurrection, at the close of Holy Week; many Filipino families are Catholic.
entries.dateRule: First Sunday after the first ecclesiastical full moon on or after March 21 (Western calendar).
entries.whatItMarks: The resurrection of Jesus in Western Christian tradition.

entries.name: Good Friday
entries.capsule: Holy Week's solemn Friday marking the crucifixion; a regular holiday in the Philippines.

dates.source: Calculated: Friday before Western Easter (Easter March 28, 2027 per USCCB)
Calculated: Friday before Western Easter (Easter April 16, 2028 per USCCB)

entries.whatItMarks: The crucifixion of Jesus. In the Philippines, Maundy Thursday and Good Friday are both regular holidays.

entries.name: Ash Wednesday
entries.capsule: Start of Lent in the Catholic calendar, 46 days before Easter.
entries.whatItMarks: The beginning of Lent, a season of fasting and penance before Easter.

entries.name: Philippine Independence Day
entries.capsule: The Philippines' national day, June 12, marking the 1898 declaration of independence from Spain.
entries.whatItMarks: The declaration of Philippine independence from Spain in 1898; a regular holiday in the Philippines.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: No 2026 Minnesota observance was found. The Philippine Consulate General in Chicago, which serves Minnesota, invited the state in November 2025 to join 2026 events for the 80th anniversary of Philippines-U.S. diplomatic relations.

sources.title: PH Consulate General in Chicago strengthens engagement with Minnesota Secretary of State

entries.name: Christmas
entries.capsule: Dec. 25, the heart of a long Filipino Christmas season of Masses, caroling, children's programs and food.
entries.whatItMarks: The birth of Jesus. In the Philippines, Dec. 24 and Dec. 31 were also declared non-working days for 2026.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Through a season of community events: Simbang Gabi Masses before Christmas (Filipino Catholic Community of Minnesota), the Fil-Minnesotan Association's Paskong Pilipino for children (since 1976), and the Cultural Society of Filipino Americans' Pasko sa Nayon (since 1978) and carolers, who sing at Masses and parties to raise money for causes. See separate entries.

sources.title: Cultural Society of Filipino Americans of Minnesota (MNopedia)

entries.name: EDSA People Power anniversary
entries.capsule: Feb. 25 remembers the 1986 People Power uprising that ended the Marcos dictatorship.

dates.source: Proclamation No. 1006 (Philippines): 40th anniversary, special working day

entries.whatItMarks: The 1986 EDSA People Power Revolution. The 40th anniversary in 2026 was declared a special working day in the Philippines, not a day off.

sources.title: Buhay Na Buhay (Walker Art Center), partner list including the Philippine Study Group of Minnesota

entries.name: Simbang Gabi
entries.capsule: Nine Masses before Christmas; in the Twin Cities, held in the evening at a different parish each night.
entries.dateRule: Nine days before Christmas, traditionally Dec. 16 to 24. Minnesota organizers set their own schedule each year; in 2019 the Twin Cities series ran Dec. 12 to 20 with a closing dawn Misa de Gallo on the Saturday before Christmas.

dates.source: Traditional span per OSV News in The Catholic Spirit; no 2026 Minnesota schedule found

entries.whatItMarks: A novena of Masses honoring Mary in preparation for Christmas, brought from the Philippines.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: The Filipino Catholic Community of Minnesota (formed 1995) rotated the Masses among nine metro parishes in 2019, mostly in English, with food after most Masses and 50 to 150 people a night; the Cultural Society of Filipino Americans caroled before the closing Mass. The Co-Cathedral of St. John the Evangelist in Rochester held a Simbang Gabi Mass with a children's program on Dec. 16, 2022.

entries.name: Pasko sa Nayon
entries.capsule: The Cultural Society of Filipino Americans' Christmas gathering, held since 1978, with performances, games, a bazaar and Santa.
entries.dateRule: Set each year by the Cultural Society of Filipino Americans of Minnesota, in the Christmas season.
entries.whatItMarks: Filipino Christmas traditions, shared with children and families.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Per MNopedia and GiveMN: performances, a skit, games and prizes, a bazaar of goods and food, lunch for all and a visit from Santa Claus.

sources.title: Cultural Society of Filipino Americans of Minnesota (MNopedia)

entries.name: Paskong Pilipino
entries.capsule: The Fil-Minnesotan Association's Christmas program for Filipino American children, begun in 1976.
entries.dateRule: Set each year by the Fil-Minnesotan Association.
entries.whatItMarks: Christmas, as a children's celebration of Filipino traditions.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Started in 1976 by FMA member Abe Malicsi; MNopedia shows a nativity scene at the 1980 event at Westwood Junior High in St. Louis Park. No current date found.

entries.name: Feast of the Santo Niño (Sinulog)
entries.capsule: Visayan feast of the child Jesus on the third Sunday of January, with Mass and Sinulog dancing.

dates.source: Calculated from the third-Sunday rule stated in The Catholic Spirit

entries.whatItMarks: Devotion to the Santo Niño, the child Jesus, patron honored in the Visayas.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: In January 2011, the 10th annual Sinulog Festival Mass at Guardian Angels in Oakdale drew about 400 people, with Sinulog dancers and a dinner program. No later Minnesota event was found.

sources.title: Filipinos gather to celebrate feast of Santo Niño (The Catholic Spirit)

entries.name: Philippine Day (Minnesota)
entries.capsule: The Cultural Society of Filipino Americans' big public day of dance, music, fashion, martial arts and food vendors.
entries.dateRule: Set each year by the Cultural Society of Filipino Americans of Minnesota. The 2002 event was March 24.
entries.whatItMarks: Filipino heritage, shared with the wider public; described as the largest annual Filipino gathering in Minnesota.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: At Aldrich Arena in Maplewood, with dozens of vendors and presenters, on-stage singing, dancing, fashion and martial arts, plus food, shipping and clothing vendors. MNopedia dates the first Philippine Day to 1988; Gov. Ventura's 2002 proclamation says the society had sponsored it since 1987.

sources.title: Cultural Society of Filipino Americans of Minnesota (MNopedia)
Governor Jesse Ventura proclamation, Philippine Day 2002

entries.name: Filipino American History Month
entries.capsule: October, a month to learn and share Filipino American history.

dates.source: Power 104.7 FM: 'October is Filipino history month'

entries.whatItMarks: The history and contributions of Filipino Americans.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Indigenous Roots in St. Paul hosted 'Basa, Kanta at Sayaw' (read, sing and dance) in October 2022, with readings in Tagalog and English and singing by lolas; the Filipino Association at Macalester held a panel of Twin Cities Filipino chefs on Oct. 19, 2023.

entries.name: Rizal Day
entries.capsule: Dec. 30 honors José Rizal, the Philippines' national hero; a regular holiday there.
entries.whatItMarks: The national hero José Rizal (regular holiday in the Philippines).

entries.name: All Saints' and All Souls' Days
entries.capsule: Nov. 1 and 2, days for remembering the dead; both were non-working days in the Philippines in 2026.

dates.source: Proclamation No. 1006 (Philippines): All Saints' Day 1 Nov.; 2 Nov. added as non-working day

entries.whatItMarks: Remembrance of saints and of family members who have died. The 2026 proclamation added Nov. 2 to give more time for these family activities.

entries.name: Pamana
entries.capsule: The Cultural Society's premier Filipino dance showcase, staged once every four years.
entries.dateRule: Once every four years, set by the Cultural Society of Filipino Americans of Minnesota.
entries.whatItMarks: The regional dance traditions of the Philippines, in four suites: Cordillera, Sarimanok, Abanico and Sa Nayon.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: First performed in 1981; moved to the Ames Center in Burnsville in 2009; MNopedia shows a performance on Sept. 10, 2016. No upcoming date found.

sources.title: Cultural Society of Filipino Americans of Minnesota (MNopedia)

entries.name: Pista sa Nayon (FilAmMinDak)
entries.capsule: A summer fiesta in Fargo-Moorhead drawing Filipino families from Minnesota and the Dakotas.
entries.dateRule: An annual summer weekend set by FilAmMinDak.
entries.whatItMarks: Filipino village festival traditions: dance, song and food.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: An evening program in Fargo and a next-day picnic at Gooseberry Park in Moorhead, with adobo and dinuguan, per an undated InForum report.

sources.title: 'Pista Sa Nayon' celebration in full swing in Fargo (InForum)
